news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: Chinese AI chipmaker Enflame has advanced its RMB 6.12 billion listing on Shanghai's Star Market with legal advisors Zhong Lun and DeHeng standardizing the structure.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail investors assume a headline RMB 6.12 billion AI semiconductor listing signals an immediate multi-bagger opportunity backed by elite legal and institutional advisory teams.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: Mega-tech listings on speculative tech boards are structured to unlock private equity liquidity and transfer early-stage venture risk onto public retail investors at peak cycle valuation multiples.

slides.title: Headline billions mask venture liquidity exits
slides.card_text: Retail traders view Enflame's RMB 6.12bn Star Market listing as a guaranteed growth signal. In reality, mega-tech listings on speculative growth boards transfer early-stage venture risk onto public retail investors at peak cycle valuation multiples.

slides.title: Institutional lock-in valuation decay
slides.card_text: Legal advisors standardize listing structures to maximize early-backer liquidity. As initial private equity lockup periods approach expiration, concentrated institutional supply dumps onto retail buyers, creating severe price compression across high-multiple AI semiconductor listings.

slides.title: Retail buys the order flow trap
slides.card_text: Institutional allocations secure early entry while day-one retail buyers pay inflated listing premiums. On speculative growth boards, secondary market volume is driven by institutional distribution, leaving retail traders holding illiquid shares during inevitable price corrections.

slides.title: Valuation math destroys retail capital
slides.card_text: When a semiconductor firm enters at peak multiples, a 50% drawdown requires a 100% gain just to break even. High-multiple listings missing near-term earnings guarantees compound losses rapidly as multiple compression normalizes valuations.

slides.title: Execute the post-IPO discipline
slides.card_text: Never purchase day-one tech IPO shares on speculative growth boards without verifying trailing price-to-sales ratios and institutional lock-in expiration schedules. Require at least two quarters of audited public filings before allocating capital.

slides.title: Audit before allocating principal
slides.card_text: Run this mandatory 3-point audit: First, cross-reference trailing price-to-sales against industry benchmarks. Second, map institutional lockup expiry dates to anticipate selling pressure. Third, verify actual cash flows rather than top-line listing valuations like RMB 6.12bn.
